newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea central bank intervenes to stop won's fall.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea central bank intervenes to stop won's fall.

text.p: The Bank of Korea, South Korea's central bank, intervened in mid-afternoon on Wednesday to stop the won's fall against the dollar, dealers said.
They said the bank began selling dollars at 842.50.
"The central supported the won in the afternoon as the won fell freely," said a local bank dealer.
Dealers said dollar short covering and importer settlements pushed the won down to this year's intraday low of 843.00.
The won opened the day at 837.00, and touched an intraday high of 836.60.
"Given shortages of dollar positions as a result of a slump in the nation's exports, the dollar's strength looks natural," said a foreign bank dealer.
